Tuned vs Kodi

November 19, 2026

Kodi is the free, open-source media centre, and its PVR IPTV Simple Client add-on turns it into an IPTV player. It's powerful and runs almost anywhere, but takes setting up. Tuned is built only for IPTV and works as soon as you sign in. Here is how they compare.

At a glance

KodiTuned
Where it runsWherever Kodi runs (Android, Windows, Mac, Linux and more)Android phones, tablets, Chromebooks, Android TV and Google TV
Playlist typesM3U file or link; Xtream catch-up linksXtream Codes login, M3U link, M3U file, MAC portal (live TV and guide)
TV guideXMLTV (gzip and XZ too)XMLTV guide as a list or a full grid, with reminders
Catch-upYes, several catch-up formatsYes, on Xtream servers that keep recordings
RecordingNot stated by the developerYes, the channel you are watching (Premium)
Pause and rewind live TVDepends on the input stream add-onYes, up to an hour kept on the device (Premium)
Several channels at onceNot stated by the developerNo, on purpose: one stream connection at a time
Casting to a TVNot stated by the developerChromecast
Picture-in-pictureNot stated by the developerYes
Offline downloadsNot stated by the developerFilms and episodes, whole seasons too (more than 3 at a time is Premium)
Profiles and parental controlsKodi's own profilesUp to 6 profiles, kids profiles and PINs (Premium); adult categories locked behind a PIN
TraktThrough separate Kodi add-onsYes, scrobbles films and episodes (Premium)
Film and show detailsThrough Kodi's library, not the IPTV add-onTMDB ratings, trailers, cast and actor pages, saved on the device
SubtitlesNot stated by the developerFull caption styling, timing fix, and subtitle search for films and episodes
AdsNoneNone, ever
PriceFree and open sourceFree; Premium US$9.99 a year with a 7-day trial, or US$24.99 once

"Not stated by the developer" means we couldn't find it on the developer's own pages or store listing. It may still be there, so check before you rule it out.

Price

Kodi and the IPTV Simple Client are free and open source (GPL-2.0). Tuned is free too; Premium is US$9.99 a year with a 7-day trial or US$24.99 once.

Tuned's prices are what Google Play charges in the United States; Play shows them in your own currency. Premium covers up to three devices, and a Tuned account can add more.

Where Kodi is ahead

  • Free and open source, with nothing to unlock.
  • Runs almost anywhere, including Windows, Mac and Linux.
  • Endlessly extendable with add-ons and skins.

Where Tuned is ahead

  • No setup. Type your Xtream login or paste a link and you're watching. Kodi needs the add-on, its settings and a guide set up by hand.
  • Films and shows from an Xtream login, sorted with TMDB pages, ready to play.
  • Pause and rewind on every live channel, recording and offline downloads, built in.
  • Made for a phone as well as a TV.

What Tuned does that most players don't

  • Opens straight to your channels. The playlist and guide live on the device, so the app shows channels the moment it opens and keeps them fresh in the background. Lists page straight from the database, so a playlist with tens of thousands of streams scrolls smoothly.
  • One stream connection, ever. The player, downloads, recordings, channel scans and backup copies take turns on a single connection, and anything in the background waits while you watch. Providers limit connections per account, and Tuned never uses a second one.
  • Live events from your guide. Today's games and fights are pulled out of the guide into one page. Tune finds a working English stream for an event, one channel at a time, and you can follow a team, league or fighter to get an alert before they play.
  • Backup copies and dead channels. When a channel has several copies, Tuned tries the next one if the first won't play, and a channel scan hides channels that never work, without blaming them for a slow internet connection or a busy server.
  • Real names over numbers. Episodes show their real titles from TMDB rather than "S1 E1", and tapping an actor opens everything they've been in, with what's in your playlist marked.
  • Sign in on a TV with your phone. Scan a QR code on the TV and type the login on your phone instead of with the remote.

Which one to pick

If you like building your own setup, or need Windows or Linux, Kodi is great and free. If you want IPTV to just work on Android and Android TV, try Tuned.

Checked on 19 November 2026. Features and prices change, so check the developer's page before you buy.
